question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?
expect: LLTO-2, 86.2% (LLTO-0.5 85.5%, LLTO-1 57.2%) vs 56.6% pristine (p10.L22-25); the thicker 2 mol.% layer suppressed electron transfer (p10.L17-20)
rendered: According to the document, the LLTO coating with 0.5 mol.% retained 85.5% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, while the pristine NCM retained 56.6%. The 2 mol.% coating decreased the rate capability, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.
